summary: 1. 2026-09-29 (same-day deep-search follow-up, prompted by Peter after the dashboard pass below) — Maaden's official September production summary surfaces a third, unreconciled YTD-shortfall figure; September's own tonnage lands almost exactly on the recovery plan's target while missing Maaden's separate FCST baseline by 15% Key operational findings 1. 2. Peter flagged that files had changed since the dashboard-scoped pass below started, and asked for a deeper search across other files and emails. 3. A full re-scan of everything under `RAW/` modified since the dashboard pass's own read window found two genuinely new items: Maaden's official September Physical Summary (client-issued, sent as a site-wide notice and forwarded internally by new Project Manager Joe Coleman), and a second post-blast grade-control drawing (`860_B520_post blast_1st.pdf`, registered cross-check only). 4. The two files the dashboard pass actually sourced its Sep 28 KPIs from (the Client Meeting Report and Daily Availability Final Report) were confirmed unchanged since they were read — no correction needed to that pass's figures. 2. 5. September's Total Tonnes Mined (1,618,708 t) landed within 1.2% of the internal recovery plan's own 1,600,000 t September target — set back on 9-Sep in [[august-2026-performance-review-escalation]] — the first month of that recovery profile essentially hitting its number, with mine grade beating Maaden's forecast by 102%. 3. 6. Against Maaden's own separate official FCST baseline (1,914,622 t), the same September figure misses by -295,914 t (-15%) — a materially different bar than the recovery-plan target, with the gap between the two baselines itself unexplained in this KB's record. 7. A third YTD-shortfall figure now circulates alongside the two already tracked. 8. The 27-Sep weekly HSE meeting's "470,000 tonnes behind YTD" and new PM Joe Coleman's own rough "roughly 800,000 tonnes behind" estimate (explicitly flagged by Coleman himself as needing verification) now sit alongside the official summary's own YTD variance of -295,914 t (-2%). 9. None of the three reconcile. This is logged as an open, unresolved question in both [[august-2026-performance-review-escalation]] and [[daily-production-report]] — not resolved here. Coleman has called a 2-3 PM meeting the same day with Bud de Quay, Joy Mpinyuri, Peter Anthony, and Muhammad Usman specifically to reconcile the figures, names October-November as the year's two hardest months, and commits to reviewing Eben Pienaar's existing recovery plan alongside the new numbers. The outcome of that meeting is the natural next update to [[august-2026-performance-review-escalation]]. The Spatial Compliance row in the source PDF's text extraction reads as a possible 0%-vs-100% miss, but the extraction is ambiguous on this specific row — flagged for a direct visual check rather than treated as confirmed. Wiki articles touched: [[august-2026-performance-review-escalation]] (new dated section, bumped to `Last updated: 2026-09-29`), [[daily-production-report]] (cross-reference added to open questions). Tasks: none created this pass — the three-way YTD-shortfall contradiction is logged as an open question rather than dispatched as an action item, since Coleman's own same-day meeting is already in motion to address it. No content removed or renamed from RAW. ---
